blocks.content: The Fundamental Duties serve as a reminder to the citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also be conscious of duties they owe to their country, their society and to their fellow citizens.

rows: Applies to Citizens and Foreigners (certain rights)
Applies exclusively to Citizens of India

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Duties were incorporated into Part IV-A of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendations.
Inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR, India is one of the few democratic nations alongside Japan to explicitly feature citizen duties in its Constitution.
The 11th Fundamental Duty (duty of a parent/guardian to provide education to children aged 6 to 14) was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2002.
Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and non-enforceable directly by courts, though Parliament can enact laws to enforce them.
These duties apply exclusively to citizens of India and do not extend to foreign nationals residing in the country.
Swaran Singh Committee recommended 8 Fundamental Duties, but the 42nd Amendment Act incorporated 10 duties into the Constitution.
The duty to pay taxes was recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee but was NOT included in the Fundamental Duties.
The Verma Committee (1999) identified existing legal sanctions for enforcing several Fundamental Duties (e.g., Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, Wildlife Protection Act).
Fundamental Duties are confined only to citizens and do not apply to foreigners, unlike certain Fundamental Rights.
